subject: Enterprise access handoff: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist, and service-account sequencing
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@globex.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Enterprise access handoff: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist, and service-account sequencing

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture a concise handoff plan for onboarding Globex with Redwood and surface the sequencing decisions we recommend so CS/engineering can avoid last-minute surprises. High-level goals: secure SSO provisioning, scoped SCIM sync for groups, explicit IP allowlist cutover windows, and a deterministic service-account provisioning pattern for automated jobs.

Proposed sequencing (short):
- Week 0 (this week): Mutual action plan signoff + inventory of identity providers and admin owners.
- Week 1: SAML test in staging (IdP metadata + assertion mapping).
- Week 2: SCIM minimal sync (users + two groups) to validate mapping and rate limits.
- Week 3: IP allowlist staging cutover + test traffic.
- Week 4: Service accounts & org policy enforcement (role scoping, ephemeral leases).

Open questions for Globex:
1) Can you confirm the IdP metadata and the SAML attribute names we should map for role assignment?
2) Do you have a preferred CIDR ranges for egress where our runtime will call back to your services?
3) Which team will own service-account rotation: Security or Infra?

Attaching a draft mutual action plan (MMP) with tasks and owners — Monica will lead the CS coordination and Ben will lead engineering runbook items. I’ll track the DocuSign/contract step if needed.

Next step: Alice, if you can confirm owners and the preferred weekend for allowlist testing, we’ll lock dates.

Thanks,
Priyom
Sr. Technical Program Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan_Globex_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)]

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@globex.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@globex.com, infra-team@globex.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:03:14 -04:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise access handoff: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist, and service-account sequencing

Hi Priyom —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side:

- IdP metadata: I uploaded the latest metadata to our shared drive and pasted a link in the MMP notes. We are on Okta; primary attributes are email (user.email) and groups (groups). We will need group->role mapping for two roles: "developer" and "operator."
- CIDR ranges: infra-team prefers testing from 34.210.0.0/18 and 54.182.0.0/16 for staging. Prod ranges will be narrower; will provide next week.
- Service-account ownership: Security prefers to author and Infra will operate rotation, but we can be flexible.

Two asks before we sign the MMP:
1) Sample SAML assertion mapping you plan to use (attribute names).
2) A short runbook for emergency rollback if SCIM imports accidentally create large groups.

We can do the allowlist test weekend of July 10-11.

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Identity Architect
Globex Corporation

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@globex.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:47:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise access handoff: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist, and service-account sequencing

Thanks Alice — great context. I updated the attached MMP with owners, acceptance criteria, and the July 10-11 test window. Quick notes for CS ops:

- Acceptance criteria for SAML staging: successful Assertion Consumer Service response, mapped groups present in staging, and login for 3 test users (dev/operator).
- SCIM minimal sync: target two groups (devs, operators), verify that we do not map any admin flags by default, and run at low throttle (60 req/min) to surface rate limits.
- Rollback plan (short): we will run SCIM in "dry-run" mode first and validate delta in the staging tenant. If anything unexpected shows up, we will toggle the provisioning connector to OFF and delete the delta via the staging admin UI; Monica will coordinate with Alice for the restore window.

Action items assigned in the sheet:
- Monica: schedule CS playbook run and confirm test users (due 2026-07-02)
- Ben: provide SA naming convention and short runbook for ephemeral keys (due 2026-07-01)
- Priyom: lock dates and update HubSpot (done)

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan_Globex_v1.xlsx (updated, 26KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@globex.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:18:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise access handoff: SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist, and service-account sequencing

Quick technical inputs from infra:

- SAML attribute mapping (recommended):
  - NameID -> user.email
  - groups -> groups (we will map strings to role names: "globex:dev" -> developer, "globex:ops" -> operator)
  - entitlements (if present) -> we will ignore for now

- SCIM considerations: we will run provisioning with incremental sync and a staging dry-run first. Our connector supports batching at 50 users per call; we recommend a 1-hour window for the first live sync.

- Service-account naming convention (see attached): redwood-glx-<env>-<purpose>-<seq> (examples: redwood-glx-prod-ingest-01, redwood-glx-stg-worker-02). Ephemeral keys: we recommend issuing short-lived tokens (TTL 8 hours) and rotating with automated job from your Vault.

- IP allowlist: staging testing OK for 34.210.0.0/18 and 54.182.0.0/16. For production please provide a finalized list; we will only accept CIDR blocks no larger than /16 for external ranges.

Attaching a short guide for SA naming and rotation.

Ben Carter
Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: sa-naming-guide.md (plain text, 3KB)]
